clue.text: Homeland for South Africans no longer — rank site abandoned

definitions.text: Homeland for South Africans no longer

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters of the two words are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A former South African homeland is described as a place where rank was left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges RANKSITE. The definition is fair because Transkei ceased to exist as a homeland in 1994.
explanation.definitionFit: Transkei was one of the apartheid-era bantustans, a nominally independent black homeland reabsorbed into South Africa in 1994.

clue.text: Like characters lined up ready for a run-off?

definitions.text: Like characters lined up ready for a run-off?

parts.words: Like characters lined up ready for a run-off?
parts.note: sounds like competitors in a race lined up for a deciding heat, but means letters arranged by a printer ready to be printed off

explanation.surface: Contestants are lined up for a deciding race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' are letters of type, and a 'run-off' is a print run, not a tie-breaking contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that has been typeset has its characters arranged for printing, ready for the press run.

clue.text: A hollow victory making one bristle

indicators.note: hollow means the middle of the word is emptied out

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: An empty triumph makes someone bristle with irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' empties WIN of its middle letter, leaving WN. 'bristle' looks like a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is the stiff bristle growing from the husk of grasses such as barley.

clue.text: Sticky paper in nasty patches around child's bed

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the bed
nasty suggests something messed up, so the letters of the word are scrambled

parts.note: a cot is a baby's bed

explanation.surface: Adhesive tape is used in unpleasant patches round a cot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' scrambles the letters to SCHTAPE, which 'around' wraps round the bed. Scotch tape is the American brand name for clear sticky tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch tape is a brand of clear adhesive tape, a sticky paper strip in everyday use.

clue.text: Group of men voicing final words

indicators.note: Group of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A group of men speaks some closing lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from 'men' into 'voicing'.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is the short closing stanza of a poem, its concluding words.

clue.text: Magic text he removed from the chambers

indicators.note: removed from tells us the word he is taken out of the word the, leaving a single letter

parts.note: antra is the plural of antrum, an anatomical cavity or chamber

explanation.surface: Someone has taken a book of spells out of the rooms where it was kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he removed from the' leaves T; ANTRA (Latin plural of antrum, a body cavity) follows it. 'the chambers' looks like one phrase, but 'the' belongs to the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantra is a Hindu or Buddhist scripture dealing with ritual, mystical and magical practices.

clue.text: A day to be wondrously overwhelmed

parts.note: Wed is the short form of Wednesday, a day of the week

explanation.surface: Someone expects a single day to leave them filled with wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be awed is to be filled with wonder and reverence, overwhelmed by something marvellous.

clue.text: Difficult literary work given investment of foreign cash

indicators.note: investment is clothing or wrapping, so the work is wrapped around the money placed inside it

parts.note: a tome is a large book
roubles are Russian currency

explanation.surface: A hard-going book receives an injection of overseas money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' is used in its old sense of clothing or enclosing, not finance, so the money is wrapped inside the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Something troublesome causes difficulty or bother, so it means hard to deal with.

clue.text: Notice academic robes, say, in lecture?

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
academic robes are an example of dress, clothing worn for an occasion

explanation.surface: Someone notices academic gowns being worn at a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. 'Notice' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech given to an audience, much like a lecture.

clue.text: Castle is prepared for Greek play.

indicators.note: prepared suggests made ready or processed, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A castle is made ready to stage a Greek drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges CASTLE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcestis is a tragedy by Euripides about the queen who dies in her husband's place.

clue.text: Evil. Londoner apt to wander round one of the capital's thoroughfares

indicators.note: letters that wander round drift out of their places, so the three words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A wicked Londoner tends to roam the streets of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wander round' rearranges EVIL, LONDONER and APT together. Pentonville Road is a road in north London, also familiar as a square on the London Monopoly board.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentonville Road is a real street running through Islington in London, so it is one of the city's roads.

clue.text: With lowly editors gathered around, writer signs

indicators.note: gathered around means the editors surround the writer, placing one piece inside the other

parts.note: subs are sub-editors, the junior staff below the editors
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A writer surrounded by junior newspaper staff puts his name to something.
explanation.walkthrough: On a newspaper, a sub (sub-editor) is a junior who checks and trims copy, hence 'lowly editors'.
explanation.definitionFit: To subscribe is to sign one's name, especially at the foot of a document, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Crazy place — it offers sweet food

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
Pl is the abbreviation for place in addresses

explanation.surface: A mad venue boasts that it serves desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offers' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is a dessert of a halved banana with ice cream and toppings, a sweet dish.

clue.text: French cleric has fat Bible with odd bits dropping out

indicators.note: dropping the odd bits means letters one, three, five and seven go, keeping only the even-placed letters

explanation.surface: A French priest owns a thick, heavy Bible that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with odd bits dropping out' keeps the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of FAT BIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is the French title for an abbot or any clergyman, so it is a French cleric.

clue.text: Disrespectful scoundrel clutching Queen, a politician

indicators.note: clutching means the scoundrel holds the queen inside

parts.note: a dog is a contemptible fellow
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A rude villain grabs hold of the Queen and a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disrespectful' could be read as describing the scoundrel, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks belittle someone, showing a lack of respect.

clue.text: Handicapped boy losing energy in brief period

parts.note: tiny means very small or brief

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word beside it

parts.note: a time is a period
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A disabled lad runs out of energy within a short spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes E out of TIME to give TIM. Tiny Tim is the crippled son of Bob Cratchit in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Tiny Tim walks with a crutch, the classic literary example of a disabled boy.

clue.text: Shrub chap discovered on good ramble.

parts.note: a man is a chap
to rove is to wander or ramble

explanation.surface: A fellow found a bush while out on a pleasant walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangrove is a tropical tree or shrub that grows in coastal swamps.

clue.text: Mythical hero useless to the people here

annotationWithheld.why: Mythical hero useless to the people here (7), as held and as the scan prints it: THESE + US covers 'the people here', but no parse accounts for 'useless' honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: Mythical hero useless to the people here

clue.text: See the most important person making a bolt

explanation.surface: Look at the boss building himself a fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' and 'making' are link words between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is both the central figure in an organisation and a large bolt serving as a pivot, as in a vehicle's steering.

clue.text: Similar sort wanting a revolution?

parts.note: a kind is a sort
a red is a revolutionary communist, someone who wants a revolution

explanation.surface: A like-minded type is looking for an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Similar' might seem a modifier of 'sort', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means alike or related in character, as in kindred spirits.

clue.text: Swank giving news when all the actors are ill?

definitions.text: news when all the actors are ill?

explanation.surface: Boasting is what you tell people when the whole cast is sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: if every actor is ill, the show is off.
explanation.definitionFit: To swank is to boast or flaunt oneself, which is exactly what a braggart does; a cancelled performance is literally a show off.

clue.text: Congress in Africa brought in very good money

indicators.note: brought in means the congress is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: fine means very good
the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

explanation.surface: An African conference took in a lot of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress in Africa' is one piece, the South African political party, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance means money or funds, as in raising finance for a project.

clue.text: Head for loch

explanation.surface: Make your way towards a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A ness is a headland or promontory, and Ness is the name of a well-known Scottish loch.

clue.text: A scarce nut is unusual life form with hard case

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters of the phrase are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A rare nut is described as an odd creature in a tough shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is unusual' rearranges A SCARCE NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, lobsters and shrimps are crustaceans, animals protected by a hard exoskeleton.

clue.text: Brownish primates climbing one gets trapped

indicators.note: gets trapped means the one is caught inside the other piece
in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: apes are primates
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Brown monkeys scale a tree and one of them is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns APES into SEPA, and 'gets trapped' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colour, named after the cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Extravagant love for emperor

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extravagant
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A ruler is shown lavish affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors, beginning with Otto the Great.

clue.text: Member of the family in favour of sister keeping nothing: say who?

parts.note: a relative is a family member
pro means in favour of

indicators.note: keeping means the sister holds the nothing inside her

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A relation supports a nun who has nothing, and someone asks who that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts O inside NUN. The definition works by example: 'who' introduces relative clauses, as in 'the man who came'.
explanation.definitionFit: Who is a standard example of a pronoun linking a clause to its noun, the grammatical class named in the answer.

clue.text: Poem due to be recited

indicators.note: to be recited means spoken out, so we go by how the word is pronounced

parts.note: money due is owed

explanation.surface: A verse is scheduled to be read out.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, often addressed to a person or thing.

clue.text: Disaster overwhelms extremely technocratic new company

indicators.note: overwhelms means the disaster engulfs the other piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: doom is ruin or disaster

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Ruin swamps a highly technical start-up firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives the first and last letters of 'technocratic'; the hyphenated answer is the usual spelling of an internet start-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot-com is an internet company, the kind of new business that boomed around the year 2000.

clue.text: Beautiful youth's heavenly body seen by Jupiter

explanation.surface: A handsome young man's celestial figure is spotted by the king of the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('has'). In myth Ganymede was the beautiful Trojan boy carried off by Zeus (Jupiter); the moon is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede was the Trojan youth famed for his beauty, and is also the largest moon orbiting the planet Jupiter.
